title: Repair a long-to-wide reshape that errors on repeated measurements (spread() duplicates)
source_relation: adapted: duplicate-key reshaping with an explicit loss policy (mean of non-missing values), expressed as a repair of a delivered function
difficulty_hypothesis: spread() cannot reshape duplicated id/key pairs; the modern pivot_wider() default silently returns list-columns with a warning. Repairs mis-handle missing values, ordering of rows and columns, id types and all-missing ids.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The superseded spread()/gather() verbs and the pivot_wider(values_fn =) replacement are tidyr-version-specific; documentation for the installed tidyr states the duplicate-handling behaviour. Base R remains a complete fallback, and the runtime error and warning both name values_fn.
mcp_relevance.information_need: How the installed tidyr handles duplicate keys and what pivot_wider's values_fn does.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: partly: spread() error text names the shared keys; pivot_wider's warning names values_fn; base R aggregate/tapply works

pinned_evidence.observed: spread() on duplicated id/key pairs errors: Each row of output must be identified by a unique combination of keys
pinned_evidence.oracle: base-R loops over sorted ids and keys; mean of non-missing values per cell
